study type: Prospective cohort study with a case-control comparison
exposure: Perceived accessibility to facility care (delays in seeking care, financial barriers)
Perceived quality of facility care (15 domains)
cohort: The study included 174 women who experienced maternal near-miss complications (cases) and 151 matched controls from Zanzibar's referral hospital.
finding: Patients with maternal near-miss complications, compared to matched controls, had less formal education, perceived their wealth as poor, experienced a higher rate of stillbirth, and encountered more financial barriers in reaching care, despite generally high perceived quality of facility care.
